512.title: Pediatric abusive head trauma
512.reference: Hymel KP, Armijo-Garcia V, Foster R, et al. Validation of a clinical prediction rule for pediatric abusive head trauma. Pediatrics 2014; 134: e1537-e1544.
512.population: Children < 3 years with acute head injury admitted to a pediatric ICU. Patients were 76% white, 60% male, and had mean LOS of 9 days in North American validation population.
512.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

513.title: Prostate CA: predicting recurrence and mortality (CAPRA-S)
513.reference: Punnen S, Freedland SJ, Presti JC, et al. Multi-institutional validation of the CAPRA-S score to predict disease recurrence and mortality after radical prostatectomy. Eur Urology 2014; 65: 1171-7.
513.population: Validated in multi-center population of 2670 men undergoing radical prostatectomy from 2001 to 2011 with mean follow-up of 58 months. All were treated at one of four VA medical centers in the US. Mean age 62 years, 58% white, 42% Gleason 2 - 6, 35% Gleason 3 + 4, 12% Gleason 4 + 3, and 11% Gleason 8 - 10.
513.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
513.comment: Prevalence refers to rate of recurrence at median of 14 months.

514.title: Lung CA: COPD Lung Cancer Screening Score
514.reference: de-Torres JP, Wilson DO, Sanchez-Salcedo P, et al. Lung cancer in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2015; 191: 285-91.
514.population: Validated in separate cohort enrolled in lung cancer screening program between 2001 and 2013 in Europe. All were 40 years or older with at least 10 pack years and no symptoms of lung cancer, and all had COPD.
514.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

515.title: Breast CA: risk of cancer in women with breast symptoms
515.reference: Galvin R, Joyce D, Downey E, et al. Development and validation of a clinical prediction rule to identify suspected breast cancer: a prospective cohort study. BMC Cancer 2014 Oct 3;14:743. doi: 10.1186/1471-2407-14-743
515.population: Developed (women presenting 3/2011 to 6/2012) and validated (women presenting 7 - 12/2012) in population of Irish women referred for evaluation of breast symptoms. Most common symptoms were lump (50%) and mastalgia (33%). Mean age 44 years, range 18 to 97 years.
515.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

516.title: Pancreatic resection prognosis (PREPARE score)
516.reference: Uzunoglu FG, Reeh M, Vettorazzi E, et al. Preoperative pancreatic resection (PREPARE) score: a prospective multicenter-based morbidity risk score. Ann Surg 2014; 260: 857-64.
516.population: Developed in 8 hospitals in Germany and Italy, with rule developed using 2005 to 2011 data and validated with 2011 to 2013 data. About half undergoing resection for cancer, 15% for adenoma, and 12% for chronic pancreatitis.
516.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation
516.comment: Prevalence refers to those with Grade III or higher complications.

517.title: Pleural infection prognosis (RAPID score)
517.reference: Rahman NM, Kahan BC, Miller RF, et al. A clinical score (RAPID) to identify those at risk for poor outcome at presentation in patients with pleural infection. Chest 2014; 145: 848-55.
517.population: Developed from patients in a multicenter pleural sepsis trial and validated in a similar trial population. Mean age 59 years, 72% male, 41% with symptoms > 14 days.
517.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

518.title: Acute stroke mortality and length of stay (SOAR stroke score)
518.reference: Kwok CS, Clark AB, Musgrave SD, et al. The SOAR stroke score predicts hospital length of stay in acute stroke: an external validation study. Int J Clin Pract 2015; 69: 659-65.
518.population: Validated in a cohort of patients with acute stroke admitted between 2008 and 2011 in Norwich, England. Mean age 77 years, 92% ischemic stroke, 38% anterior circulation stroke.
518.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
518.comment: Prevalence refers to mortality at discharge.

519.title: Panic disorder screening (PHQ PRIME-MD)
519.reference: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JB, et al. Validation and utility of a self-report version of PRIME-MD: The PHQ Primary Care Study. JAMA 1999; 282: 1737-44.
519.population: Validated in 8 primary care sites from 1997 to 1998 in adult patients, mean age 46 years and range 18 to 99 years, with 66% female and 79% white.
519.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

520.title: Delirium diagnosis: 3D-CAM tool
520.reference: Marcantonio ER, Ngo LH, O'Connor M, et al. 3D-CAM: derivation and validation of a 3 minute diagnostic interview for CAM-defined delirium. Ann Intern Med 2014; 161: 554-61.
520.population: Validated prospectively in 201 hospitalized adults with mean age 84 years, 28% of whom had dementia.
520.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

521.title: Pancreatectomy readmission prediction (RAP score)
521.reference: Valero V, Grimm JC, Kilic A, Lewis RL, et al. A novel risk scoring system reliably predicts readmission after pancreatectomy. J Am Coll Surg 2015; 220: 701-13.
521.population: Developed and validated (random split sample) using a retrospective analysis of patients undergoing pancreatectomy at one of 9 high volume centers between 2005 and 2011. Mean age 63 years, 52% female, 68% undergoing Whipple, and 61% with malignant pathology.
521.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

522.title: Hepatic resection readmission prediction (RRS)
522.reference: Egger, ME, Squires MH, Kooby DA, et al. Risk stratification for readmission after major hepatectomy: development of a readmission risk score. J Am Coll Surg 2015; 220: 640-8.
522.population: Developed and validated (random split sample) using a retrospective cohort of patients undergoing hepatectomy at one of 3 US academic medical centers. Most were undergoing surgery for malignancy (77%), mean age 58 years.
522.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

523.title: Pulmonary nodule prognosis in colorectal cancer
523.reference: Kim CH, Huh JW, Kim HR, Kim YJ. Indeterminate pulmonary nodules in colorectal cancer: follow-up guidelines based on a risk predictive model. Ann Surg 2015; 261: 1145-52.
523.population: Developed in Korean patients who underwent surgery from 2008 to 2010, and validated in a smaller group from the same population. In validation set, mean age 70 years, 55% male. Overall, 27% had an indeterminate pulmonary nodule.
523.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

524.title: Clostridium difficile: prediction of severe infection
524.reference: Na X, Martin AJ, Sethi S, et al. A multi-center prospective derivation and validation of a clinical prediction tool for severe clostridium difficile infection. PLOS One 2015. 10(4): e0123405.doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0123405
524.population: Developed among inpatients in Boston and validated among inpatients in Houston, Texas and Dublin, Ireland. Mean age 66 years, 50% male, 16% with prior episode of c. diff infection.
524.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

525.title: DVT diagnosis in pregnancy (LEFt score)
525.reference: Moigne E, Genty C, Meunier J, et al. Validation of the LEFt score, a newly proposed diagnostic tool for deep vein thrombosis in pregnant women. Thrombosis Research 2014; 134: 664-7.
525.population: Validated in 3 studies of pregnant women referred for clinical suspicion of DVT
525.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
525.comment: In the Moigne study population, probability of DVT was 3.3%, 8.6%, 10% and 75% for 0, 1, 2 and 3 points. Primary value is when score = 0.

526.title: Legionella probability in community-acquired pneumonia
526.reference: Haubitz S, Hitz F, Graedel L, et al. Ruling out legionella in community-acquired pneumonia. Am J Med 2014; 127: 1010.e11-1010.e19
526.population: Validated in a group of 1939 patients with CAP from an international database, of whom 29% had a confirmed final diagnosis.
526.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

527.title: Children with fever and cough: low risk score for pneumonia
527.reference: Oostenbrink R, Thompson M, Lakhanpaul M, et al. Children with fever and cough at emergency care: diagnostic accuracy of a clinical model to identify children at low risk of pneumonia. Eur J Emerg Med 2013; 20: 273-80.
527.population: Developed in pediatric ED in Rotterdam, Netherlands and validated in two pediatric EDs in UK. Mean age 2.3 years, 47% male, with 7% in one hospital and 14% in another diagnosed with pneumonia based on chest radiographs.
527.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
527.comment: Prevalence is percent with pneumonia in validation population.

528.title: Appendicitis: ruling out in adults with indeterminate USN
528.reference: Leeuwenburgh MM, Stockman HB, Bouma WH, et al. A simple clinical decision rule to rule out appendicitis in patients with nondiagnostic ultrasound results. Acad Emerg Med 2014; 21: 488-96.
528.population: Developed and validated in patients presenting to the ED with suspected appendicitis. Validated in patients with negative or indeterminate ultrasound. In validation group, median age 35 years, 39% males, 77% with duration < 2 days, and 57% with inconclusive or negative ultrasound.
528.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

529.title: Low back pain: likelihood of rapid recovery
529.reference: Williams CM, Hancock MJ, Maher CG, McAuley JH, et al. Predicting rapid recovery from acute low back pain based on the intensity, duration, and history of pain: a validation study. Eur J Pain 2014; 18: 1182-9.
529.population: Validated in 937 patients who were enrolled in a primary care study of acetaminophen for low back pain. Mean age 44 years, 46% female, 22% with pain referred distal to knee, and mean of 11 previous episodes and mean duration 10 days.
529.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
529.comment: Prevalence is proportion not recovered at 12 weeks

530.title: Acute coronary syndrome prognosis (MACS score)
530.reference: Body R, Carley S, McDowell G, et al. The Manchester Acute Coronary Syndromes (MACS) decision rule for suspected cardiac chest pain: derivation and external validation. Heart 2014; 100: 1462-8.
530.population: Developed at Manchester Royal Infirmary and validated in suburban general hospital in Stockport, UK. Mean age 64 years, 58% male, 30% previous MI, 22% previous PCI.
530.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

531.title: Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale
531.reference: Han JH, Vasilevskis EE, Schnelle JF, et al. The diagnostic performance of the Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale for detecting delirium in older emergency department patients. Acad Emerg Med 2015; 22: 878-82.
531.population: Prospective validation of this score in a group of 406 patients 65+ years with dementia admitted to the ED.
531.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

532.title: Canadian TIA Prognosis Score
532.reference: Perry JJ, Sharma M, Sivilotti ML, et al. A prospective cohort study of patients with transient ischemic attack to identify high-risk clinical characteristics. Stroke 2014; 45: 92-100.
532.population: Developed in 3906 patients presenting with a stroke in the previous 7 days. Mean age 68 years, 51% women.

533.title: Colorectal cancer: risk of advanced neoplasia
533.reference: Schroy PC, Wong JB, O'Brien MJ, et al. A risk prediction index for advanced colorectal neoplasia at screening colonoscopy. Am J Gastroenterol 2015; 110: 1062-71.
533.population: Developed in 3543 asymptomatic patients 50 to 79 years of age undergoing screening colonoscopy. Age 50 to 59: 2646 patients; 50% male; 53% black.

534.title: Hepatitis C: prognosis of advanced hepatic fibrosis
534.reference: van der Meer AJ, Hansen BE, Fattovich G, et al. Reliable prediction of clinical outcome in patients with chronic HCV infection and compensated advanced hepatic fibrosis: a validated model using objective and readily available clinical parameters. Gut 2015; 64: 322-31.
534.population: Developed in a cohort of consecutive patients with Hep C infection without SVR after initial treatment. Validated in patients from EUROHEP cohort that included patients in a European cohort of patients with Hep C and biopsy proven cirrhosis.
534.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

535.title: HOSPITAL score to predict avoidable readmissions
535.reference: Donze JD, Williams MV, Robinson EJ, et al. International Validity of the HOSPITAL Score to Predict 30-Day Potentially Avoidable Hospital Readmissions. JAMA Intern Med 2016; 176: 496-502.
535.population: This was a validation study, in 117,065 consecutive discharges from a medical department in 2011. Mean age 61 years, 52% male. AUROCC = 0.72.
535.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

536.title: Screening for drug use
536.reference: Tiet QQ, Leyva YE, Moos RH, et al. Screen of Drug Use: Diagnostic accuracy of a new brief tool for primary care. JAMA Intern Med 2015; 175: 1371-7.
536.population: Patients from two primary care clinics at a VA Medical Center; 95% male, mean age 62 years, 72% high school education, 62% not married.
536.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

537.title: Avian flu (H76N9) diagnosis
537.reference: Liao Q, Ip DK, Tsang TK, et al. A clinical prediction rule for diagnosing human infections with avian influenza A (H7N9) in a hospital emergency department setting. BMC Medicine 2014; 12: 127.
537.population: Patients came from 2 databases, one of 121 lab-confirmed cases of A(H7N9) in China, and the other 2603 patients with non-H7N9 acute respiratory tract infection captured by a surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections. About half of patients in both databases were 60 years or older; 30% in the H7N9 group and 40% in the non-H7N9 group were female.
537.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

538.title: ED Assessment of Chest Pain Score and 2 Hour Protocol
538.reference: Than M, Flaws D, Sanders S, et al. Development and validation of the Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain Score and 2 h accelerated Diagnostic Protocol. Emerg Med Australasia 2014; 26: 34-44.
538.population: Consecutive adults with at least 5 minutes of pain that was felt to possibly be caused by ACS. Outcomes adjudicated blindly; mean age was 60 years and 60% were male. Outcome predicted was a major adverse cardiac event (MACE) at 30 days.
538.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

539.title: COPD mortality risk in hospital (DECAF score)
539.reference: Echevarria C, Steer J, Heslop-Marshall K, et al. Validation of the DECAF score to predict hospital mortality in acute exacerbations of COPD. Thorax 2016; 71: 133-40.
539.population: Score was developed in 1 hospital and validated in 4 others. The mean age of participants was 73 years, 54% were female, and the mean FEV1 was 45% of predicted. Goal is to predict mortality among patients hospitalized for acute exacerbation of COPD.
539.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
539.comment: Rule was 100% sensitive and 59% specific in the validation cohort

540.title: UGI bleed: Risk of Bad Outcome (C-WATCH score)
540.reference: Hoffmann V, Neubauer H, Heinzler J, et al. A novel easy-to-use prediction scheme for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: Cologne-WATCH (C-WATCH) Risk Score. Medicine 2015; 94(38): 1 - 7.
540.population: Score was developed to predict the composite of recurrent bleeding, need for intervention, or 30 day mortality among patients with an acute UGI bleed, before endoscopy. Mean age was 64 years, 33% female.
540.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation
540.comment: Area under ROC curve = 0.70 in validation set, 0.73 in development.

541.title: Bleeding risk in atrial fibrillation (ORBIT)
541.reference: O'Brien EC, DaJuanicia NS, Thomas LE, et al. The ORBIT bleeding score: a simple bedside score to assess bleeding risk in atrial fibrillation. Eur Heart J 2015; 36: 3258-64.
541.population: Score was developed using data from the US ORBIT-AF registry of patients with incident and prevalent atrial fibrillation. Mean age 75 years, 58% male, 89% white.
541.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.
541.comment: Area under ROC curve = 0.67, not prospectively validated. Accuracy similar to HAS-BLED and ATRIA scores in this study.

542.title: Stroke risk in patients with AF (ATRIA)
542.reference: van den Ham HA, Klungel OH, Singer DE, et al. Comparative performance of ATRIA, CHADS2, and CHA2DS2-VASc risk scores predicting stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation. J Am Coll Cardiol 2015; 66; 17: 1851-9
542.population: Score was validated prospectively in a disease registry in the UK that includes adults 18 and older with initial diagnosis of AF between 1998 and 2012. Mean age 74 years, 51% male, 50% current or past smoker, mean follow-up of 2.8 years.
542.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

543.title: Acute coronary syndrome prognosis (HEART score)
543.reference: Fanaroff AC, Rymer JA, Goldstein SA, et al. Does this patient with chest pain have acute coronary syndrome? The Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review. JAMA 2015; 314: 1955-65.
543.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
543.comment: LR ranged from 0.20 for low risk to 13 for high risk. Likelihood of ACS ranged from 2.9% to 66%.

544.title: Serious infection risk in children and adolescents (ERNIE)
544.reference: Van den Bruel A, et al. Signs and symptoms for diagnosis of serious infections in children: a prospective study in primary care. Br J Gen Pract 2007; 57(540): 538-546.
544.population: Score was developed and internally validated in 3981 children presenting to a GP or ED in Flanders, Belgium with up to 5 days of acute illness. Reference standard was review of records of hospitalization in region and personal contact with all treating physicians. Mean age 5.0 years.
544.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

545.title: Pneumonia risk in children with cough (STARWAVE)
545.reference: Hay A, et al. Development and internal validation of a clinical rule to improve antibiotic use in children presenting to primary care with acute respiratory tract infection and cough: a prognostic cohort study. Lancet Respir Med 2016; 4: 902-10.
545.population: Score was developed and internally validated in a group of 8394 children age 3 months to 16 years presenting to their GP in the UK with a chief complaint of cough and suspected respiratory tract infection of less than 28 days duration. Median age 3 years, IQ range 1 to 6 years, 52% male.
545.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

546.title: Risk of post-concussion syndrome in children with head injury
546.reference: Zemek R, et al. Clinical risk score for persistent post-concussion symptoms among children with acute concussion in the ED. JAMA 2016; 315(10): 1014-25.
546.population: The score was derived in children presenting between August, 2013 and September 2014 within 48 hours of acute head injury to one of 9 ED's, and validated in the same group of facilities during the subsequent 9 months. Median age 12 years, median time from injury to presentation 3 hours, 24% had experienced a prior concussion but only 10% had experienced more than one.
546.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

547.title: Delirium susceptibility in medical inpatients
547.reference: Pendlebury ST, Lovett NG, et al. Delirium risk stratification in consecutive unselected admissions to acute medicine: validation of a susceptibility score based on factors identified externally in pooled data for use at entry to the acute care pathway. Age and Ageing 2017; 46: 226-31.
547.population: The score was derived based on a review of the literature to identify risk factors for delirium. It was then prospectively validated in a group of 308 consecutive medical inpatients 65 years and older in Oxford, England. Mean age was 82 years, 54% female.
547.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

548.title: Drug Resistance in Pneumonia score (DRIP)
548.reference: Webb BJ, et al. Derivation and multicenter validation of the drug resistance in pneumonia clinical prediction score. Antimicrobial Agents Chemo 2016; 60(5): 2652-62.
548.population: The score was derived from 200 cases of microbiologically confirmed pneumonia admitted to one of 7 hospitals in Utah. It was prospectively validated in 200 patients at 4 tertiary care hospitals in the US, 2 of which were not part of the original derivation population. Mean age was 63 years, 41% had chronic lung disease, and 18% poor functional status with an inpatient mortality rate of 8.5%. The rate of drug resistant pathogens was 25% in the derivation group and 33% in the validation group.
548.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

549.title: Invasive bacterial infection in febrile infants (Step by Step rule)
549.reference: Gomez B, et al. Validation of the Step-by-Step approach in the management of young febrile infants. Pediatrics 2016; DOI: 10.1542/peds.2015-4381
549.population: This was a validation study of a previously developed rule. It was evaluated in 2185 infants at one of 11 European pediatric ED's. All participants were less than 90 days old and presented with fever without a clear source. The median age was 47 days, and 17% were less than 21 days old. The mean duration of fever was 5 hours, and 86% were previously healthy and classified as well appearing on arrival.
549.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

550.title: Pneumonia in outpatients with cough (GRACE rule)
550.reference: van Vugt S, Broekhuizen BD, et al. Use of serum C reactive protein and procalcitonin concentrations in addition to symptoms and signs to predict pneumonia in patients presenting to primary care with acute cough: diagnostic study. BMJ 2013; 346: f2450 doi 10.1136/bmj.f2450
550.population: The score was derived from a population of 2820 adults in 12 countries presenting to their primary care physician with an acute cough who all had a CXR as the reference standard. Their mean age was 50 years, 40% were men, and 33% had a severe cough.
550.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

554.title: UTI diagnosis in children < 5 years (DUTY)
554.reference: Hay AD, Sterne JA, Hood K, et al. Improving the diagnosis and treatment of urinary tract infection in young children in primary care: results from the DUTY prospective diagnostic cohort study. Ann Fam Med 2016; 14: 325-36.
554.population: The score was derived and internally validated using data from 2740 children presenting with at least one constitutional symptom of UTI (fever, vomiting, lethargy, irritability, poor feeding or failure to thrive) and at least 1 UTI specific symptoms (abdominal pain, jaundice in children < 3 mos, hematuria, offensive urine odor, cloudy urine, loin pain, frequency, apparent pain on passing urine, and changes in continence).

555.title: Heart failure diagnosis using proBNP (Dutch Kelder rule)
555.reference: Kelder JC, Cramer MJ, et al. The diagnostic value of physical examination and additional testing in primary care patients with suspected heart failure. Circulation 2011; 124: 2865-73.
555.population: Derived from adults with signs and symptoms sugggesting heart failure, most commonly dyspnea, fatigue, and edema or crackles presenting to a GP in the Netherlands. All underwent a standard diagnostic work-up including ECG, spirometry, blood tests, and an echocardiogram. Reference standard was a consensus judgement of a panel blinded to proBNP result but having all other data. It was validated in two similar UK datasets.
555.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
555.comment: AUROCC = 0.83 to 0.95 in the derivation and validation datasets.

556.title: Heart failure diagnosis in ED (Brest score)
556.reference: Basset A, Nowak E, Castellant P, et al. Devlopment of a clinical prediction score for congestive heart failure diagnosis in the emergency care setting: The Brest score. Am J Emerg Med 2016; 34: 2277-2283.
556.population: Derived from a consecutive retrospective cohort of adults presenting to the ED with acute dyspnea. The diagnosis of heart failure was determined by a review of all data including BNP, ECG, and echocardiogram (which were not all available for all patients). It was prospectiely validated in consecutive adults with acute dyspnea at the same institution.
556.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

557.title: Choosing DOA vs warfarin in atrial fibrillation (ENGAGE AF-TIMI score)
557.reference: Fanola C, Giugliano RP, Ruff CT, et al. A novel risk prediction score in atrial fibrillation for a net clinical outcome from the ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 randomized clinical trial. Eur Heart J 2017; 38: 888-96.
557.population: Derived from a warfarin-naïve cohort of 2898 patients randomized to edoxaban, a direct-acting oral anticoagulant, or warfarin. It was validated in 5532 other patients in the same trial. There was 3 year follow-up and both benefits and harms were tabulated. Mean age 71 years, 58% male.
557.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

558.title: Risk of colorectal cancer in symptomatic patients using FIT
558.reference: Cubiella J, Vega P, Salve M, et al. Development and external validation of a faecal immunochemical test-based prediction model for colorectal cancer detection in symptomatic patients. BMC Medicine 2016; 14: 128
558.population: Developed in 1572 patients presenting with GI symptoms and referred for colonoscopy; validated in a separate group of 1481 patients with similar indications for colonoscopy. Mean age 68 years, 51% male, 60% with rectal bleeding, 57% change in bowel habits, and 44% abdominal pain.
558.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

559.title: Mortality risk in acute lung injury (ARDS)
559.reference: Cooke CR, Shah CV, Gallop R, et al. A simple clinical predictive index for objective estimates of mortality in acute lung injury. Crit Care Med 2009; 37(6): 1913-20.
559.population: The clinical decision rule was developed in 414 patients with non-traumatic acute lung injury (ARDS), and validated in a second group of 459 patients with ARDS. The mean age was 48 years for survivors and 60 years for non-survivors, 74% were white, and 60% male. Most had pneumonia and sepsis as the underlying risk factor for acute lung injury.
559.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
559.comment: AUROCC = 0.72 in derivation cohort, 0.68 in validation cohort

560.title: Safe removal from cardiac monitoring (Ottawa Chest Pain Cardiac Monitoring Rule)
560.reference: Syed S, Gatien M, Perry JJ, et al. Prospective validation of a clinical decision rule to identify patients presenting to the emergency department with chest pain who can safely be removed from cardiac monitoring. CMAJ 2017; 189: E139-45.
560.population: Adults with chest pain presenting to the ED were prospectively enrolled to develop the model. Mean age 64 years, 56% male, and 9% ultimately admitted to hospital.
560.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

562.title: Benefit of prolonged DAPT following PCI (DAPT score)
562.reference: Yeh RW, Secemsky EA, Kereiakes DJ, et al. Development and validation of a prediction rule for benefit and harm of dual antiplatelet therapy beyond 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention. JAMA. 2016;315:1735–1749
562.population: Adults from two large clinical trials (DAPT for development, PROTECT for validation) that randomized patients to placebo or continued dual antiplatelet therapy with thienopyridine at 12 months.
562.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
562.comment: Prevalence of ischemia 3.0%, and of bleeding 1.8% in entire population

563.title: Pediatric pneumonia: likelihood of prolonged hospital stay
563.reference: Breuer O, Picard E, Benabu N, et al. Predictors of prolonged hospitalizations in pediatric complicated pneumonia. Chest 2018; 153(1): 172-180.
563.population: Developed in 144 patients and validated in 169 children hospitalized between 1997 and 2017 in one of three Israeli tertiary care hospitals. Mean age 5 years, 63% male.
563.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

564.title: Circulatory death after initial inpatient CPR survival (CREST)
564.reference: Bascom KE, Dziodzio J, Vasaiwala S, et al. Derivation and validation of the CREST Model for very early prediction of circulatory etiology death in patients without ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction after cardiac arrest. Circulation 2018; 137(3): 273 - 282.
564.population: Adult patients who were comatose following survival of attempted in-hospital CPR following an episode of cardiopulmonary arrest, at one of 44 US and European centers participating in the INTCAR registry.

565.title: Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS)
565.reference: Nazerian P, Mueller C, de Matos Soeiro A, et al. Diagnostic accuracy of the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score plus d-dimer for acute aortic syndromes: The ADvISED prospective multicenter study. Circulation 2018; 137(3): 250-258.
565.population: Developed using data from 2538 patients with acute aortic dissection presenting to one of 24 emergency departments taking part in an international registry and valued in conjunction with d-dimer testing in a prospective study of 1850 adults who had aortic syndrome (dissection, hematoma, ulcer, or rupture) in the differential diagnosis.
565.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

566.title: Prostate cancer prognosis (Cambridge Prognostic Groups)
566.reference: Gnanapragasam VJ, Bratt O, Muir K, et al. The Cambridge Prognostic Groups for improved prediction of disease mortality at diagnosis in primary non-metastatic prostate cancer: a validation study. BMC Medicine 2018 Feb 28;16(1):31. doi: 10.1186/s12916-018-1019-5.
566.population: Validation study used data for men in the Prostate Cancer data Base Sweden (PCBaSe) 3.0. It includes 72,337 men, of whom 7162 died of prostate cancer during a median 7 year follow-up period
566.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

567.title: Sepsis prognosis (SOFA score)
567.reference: Raith EP, et al. Prognostic accuracy of the SOFA score, SIRS criteria, and qSOFA score for in-hospital mortality among adults with suspected infection admitted to the intensive care unit. JAMA 2017;317(3):290-300.
567.population: Adults with suspected infection admitted to an Australian or New Zealand ICU. Mean age 63 years, 55% male, about half in a tertiary hospital.
567.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

568.title: Sepsis prognosis (qSOFA score)
568.reference: Raith EP, et al. Prognostic accuracy of the SOFA score, SIRS criteria, and qSOFA score for in-hospital mortality among adults with suspected infection admitted to the intensive care unit. JAMA 2017;317(3):290-300.

569.title: Risk of new onset AF in STEMI patients undergoing PCI (ALBO)

569.comment: AUROCC 0.73 in derivation and 0.76 in validation cohorts.

570.title: Risk of chronic kidney disease after acute kidney injury
570.reference: James MT, Pannu N, Hemmelgarn BR, et al. Derivation and external validation of prediction models for advanced chronic kidney disease following acute kidney injury. JAMA 2017; 318(18): 1787-97.
570.population: Developed in 9973 patients hospitalized from 2004 to 2014 in Alberta, Canada and then externally validated in 2761 patients in Ontario, hospitalized from 2004 to 2012. All participants had at least 1 year of follow-up.
570.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

571.title: Risk of hepatocellular cancer in patients with hepatitis C
571.reference: Xing J, Spradling PR, Moorman AC, et al. A point system to forecast hepatocellular carcinoma risk before and after treatment among persons with chronic hepatitis C. Dig Dis Sci 2017; 62: 3221-34.

571.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

572.title: Mortality in patients with suspected sepsis (CHARM)
572.reference: Chen KF, Liu SH, Li CH, et al. Development and validation of a parsimonious and pragmatic CHARM score to predict mortality in patients with sepsis. Am J Emerg Med 2017; 35: 640-6.
572.population: Developed using 2010 data and validated using 2011/12 data from Taiwanese tertiary care hospital. Patients seen in ED and who had at least 2 blood cultures ordered were included, mean age 65 years, 54% male.
572.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation
572.comment: AUROCC = 0.77, good calibration. Mortality shown is for the validation group.

573.title: Coronary artery disease in primary care patients with chest pain (INTERCHEST)
573.reference: Aerts M, Minalu G, Bosner S, et al. Pooled individual patient data from five countries were used to derive a clinical prediction rule for coronary artery disease in primary care. J Clin Epidemiol 2017; 81: 120-8.
573.population: Data from 5 studies of primary care outpatients with chest pain (n=3099). Rule was developed using 3 centers, and validated using 2 (Swiss and German, n = 1882). In validation group, mean age ~57 years, 55% female.

573.comment: Original report identified score <= 1 as low risk, with 2.3% likelihood of CAD. AUROCC = 0.84.

574.title: Predicting inpatient delirium (AWOL score)
574.reference: Brown EG, Josephson SA, Anderson N, et al. Predicting inpatient delirium: the AWOL delirium risk-stratification score in practice. Geriatric Nursing 2017; 38: 567-72.
