574.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
574.comment: AUROCC = 0.73 for incident delirium, 0.83 when prevalent cases are included.

575.title: Probability of migraine as cause of headache (POUND)
575.reference: Michel P, Henry P, et al. Diagnostic screen for assessment of the IHS criteria for migraine by general practitioners. Cephalalgia 1993; 13(suppl): 54-9.
575.population: Developed in study of 1049 French railway employees, of whom 166 had at least one headache every 3 months and were used to develop the rule.
575.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

576.title: Probability of fibrosis in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFLD Fibrosis Score)
576.reference: Angulo P, et al. The NAFLD Fibrosis Score: A noninvasive system that identifies liver fibrosis in patients with NAFLD. Hepatology 2007; 45:846-854.
576.population: Derived in a series of 733 consecutive untreated patients with NAFLD from one of 5 international centers who had liver biopsy as the reference standard test. Of the cohort, 33% had no fibrosis, 40% stage 1-2 fibrosis, and 27% stage 3-4 fibrosis.
576.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

577.title: Stroke prognosis - early mortality in acute ischemic stroke
577.reference: Gattringer T, et al. Predicting mortality of acute ischemic stroke: score-based approach. Stroke 2019; 50: 349-56.
577.population: Derived using 77,653 adults with acute ischemic stroke in an Austrian Stroke Registry, and prospectively validated in 9141 patients from 2017
577.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

578.title: Serious bacterial infection risk < 60 days: lab-based rule
578.reference: Kuppermann N, et al. A clinical prediction rule to identify febrile infants 60 days and younger at low risk for serious bacterial infections. JAMA Pediatrics 2019; 173: 342-51.
578.population: Derived on previously healthy infants presenting with fever 38 C or higher; excluded if recent antibiotics, critically ill, prematurity, pre-existing medical conditions, indwelling devices, or soft-tissue infections.
578.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

579.title: COPD : risk of bad outcomes for patients in the ED (Ottawa COPD Risk Scale)
579.reference: Stiell IG, et al. Clinical validation of a risk scale for serious outcomes among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease managed in the emergency department. CMAJ 2018; 190: E1406-13.
579.population: Derived in a cohort of 945 patients presenting to the ED with an exacerbation of COPD, and validated in a similar group. Short-term serious outcome included death within 30 days, or any of the following within 14 days: admission to a monitored unit, intubation, MI, major cardiac surgery, or return to ED.
579.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

580.title: Pulmonary embolism: diagnosis (YEARS algorithm)
580.reference: van der Hulle T, et al. Simplified diagnostic management of suspected pulmonary embolism (the YEARS study): a prospective, multicentre, cohort study. Lancet 2017; 390: 289-97.
580.population: Years algorithm was developed empirically, drawing on the Wells rule for 3 items and combining it with d-dimer. The prospective validation population consisted of adult inpatients or outpatients presenting with clinically suspected pulmonary embolism. Mean age 53 years, 62% women.
580.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

581.title: Pulmonary embolism: diagnosis in pregnancy (modified YEARS algorithm)
581.reference: van der Pol LM, et al. Pregnancy-adapted YEARS algorithm for diagnosis of suspected pulmonary embolism. N Engl J Med 2019; 380: 1139-49.
581.population: YEARS algorithm was modified based on expert opinion for pregnant adults adding the step of compression ultrasound if clinical signs of DVT to reduce need for CT. Validated in pregnant adult women presenting with new onset of worsening chest pain or dyspnea, with or without tachycardia or hemoptysis. All were followed for 3 months.
581.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

582.title: Syncope prognosis: 30 day risk of death or arrhythmia (Canadian Syncope Arrhythmia score)
582.reference: Thiruganasambandamoorthy V, et al. Predicting short-term risk of arrhythmia among patients with syncope: the Canadian Syncope Arrhythmia Risk Score. Acad Emerg Med 2017; 24: 1315-26.
582.population: Patients presenting with acute syncope were identified at 6 large emergency departments. Excluded if > 5 minutes unconsciousness, change in mental status, trauma, or seizure. Mean age 75 years, 38% female in those with serious outcome, 53 years and 55% female in those without serious event.
582.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
582.comment: Used bootstrapping with shrinkage factor applied to improve generalizability.

583.title: 1 year mortality after discharge in elderly (Bedside Risk Score)
583.reference: Walter LC, et al. Development and validation of a prognostic index for 1-year mortality in older adults after hospitalization. JAMA 2001; 285: 2987.
583.population: Derived in patients at a tertiary care hospital 70 years and older who were admitted to a general medical ward. Excluded if specialty admission, elective admission, or ICU admission. Approximately half 70 to 79 years, half 80 or older, 67% women in derivation cohort. Validated in a community hospital cohort, in validation cohort 4% were 80 years and older, 61% were women.
583.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

584.title: Cellulitis in children: need for IV antibiotics (Melbourne ASSET score)

585.title: Coronary artery disease: pretest probability (ESC guidelines)
585.reference: Genders TSS, et al. A clinical prediction rule for the diagnosis of coronary artery disease: validation, updating and extension. Eur Heart J 2011; 32: 1316-30.
585.population: The goal was to update the Diamond-Forrester pretest probabilities with a contemporary cohort of 2260 patients (1521 men and 739 women, mean age 62). Ultimately 58% were diagnosed with CAD by angiography.
585.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

586.title: Chest pain: identification of patients for early discharge (Vancouver Chest Pain Rule)
586.reference: Cullen L, et al. The new Vancouver Chest Pain Rule using troponin as the only biomarker: an external validation study. Am J Emerg Med 2014; 32: 129-34.
586.population: Validated in adults presenting with at least 5 minutes of chest pain suggestive of acute coronary syndrome, without an apparent non-cardiac source. Median age 60 years, 60% male.
586.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

587.title: Community-acquired pneumonia: risk of bacteremia
587.reference: Kim B, et al. Bacteremia prediction model for community-acquired pneumonia: external validation in a multicenter retrospective cohort. Acad Emerg Med 2017; 24: 1226-34
587.population: Validated in 2014 among patients admitted to one of 8 hospitals in Seoul, Korea with a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia. Mean age 68 years, 61% male.
587.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

588.title: Pediatric head injury: need for CT imaging (CATCH2 rule)
588.reference: Osmond MH, et al. Validation and refinement of a clinical decision rule for the use of computed tomography in children with minor head injury in the emergency department. CMAJ 2018; 190: E816-22.
588.population: Validation (with addition of 1 item) of the CATCH rule, creating CATCH2 rule in 4060 children ages 0 to 16 years presenting with minor head injury.
588.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

589.title: Febrile seizure: probability of recurrence
589.reference: Berg AT, et al. Predictors of recurrent febrile seizures: a prospective cohort study. Arch Pediatr Adolesc Med 1997; 151: 371-8.
589.population: Developed in a prospective cohort of 428 children with a first febrile seizure who were followed for at least two years.
589.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

590.title: Lower respiratory tract infection: prognosis in elderly adults
590.reference: Bont J, et al. A prediction rule for elderly primary-care patients with lower respiratory tract infections. Eur Respir J 2007; 29: 969-75
590.population: Developed in a cohort of elderly Dutch patients with a diagnosis of pneumonia, acute bronchitis, or acute exacerbation of COPD. Validated in a national cohort of Dutch GP patients.
590.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

591.title: Cholecystitis diagnosis (Bedside Score)
591.reference: Yeh, et al. Derivation and validation of a practical Bedside Score for the diagnosis of cholecystitis. Am J Emerg Med 2019; 37: 61-66.
591.population: Developed in a retrospective cohort of patients undergoing surgery for clinically suspected acute cholecystitis, validated prospectively in a cohort of patients undergoing RUQ ultrasound for clinically suspected cholecystitis at a different hospital.
591.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

592.title: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: diagnosis
592.reference: Reddy YN, et al. A simple, evidence-based approach to help guide diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Circulation 2018; 138: 861-70.
592.population: Developed in consecutive patients undergoing invasive exercise testing because of dyspnea not otherwise explained at the Mayo Clinic. Excluded if EF <50%, valvular heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or heart transplant. Validated in a similar cohort at the same institution.
592.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

593.title: Systemic sclerosis: diagnostic criteria
593.reference: van den Hoogen F, et al. 2013 classification criteria for systemic sclerosis: An American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism Collaborative Initiative. Arth Rheum 2013; 11: 2737-47.
593.population: Developed based on expert consensus process, validated against data from several cohorts of patients with systemic sclerosis, in an iterative process. From EULAR and ACR guideline committees.

594.title: Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) score for diagnosis in adults and children
594.reference: de Castro SM, et al. Evaluation of the Appendicitis Inflammatory Response Score for patients with acute appendicitis. World J Surg 2012; 36: 1540-5.
594.population: Validation study in consecutive ED patients with suspected acute appendicitis presenting between 2006 and 2009. Age range 1 to 97 years, mean age 25 years, 56% female.
594.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

595.title: Subdural hematoma: low risk criteria for further interventions
595.reference: Pruitt P, et al. A decision instrument to identify isolated traumatic subdural hematomas at low risk of neurologic deterioration, surgical intervention, or radiographic worsening. Acad Emerg Med 2017; 24: 1377-86
595.population: Developed in retrospective cohort of patients presenting to urban Level 1 trauma center with isolated subdural hematoma, validated prospectively in patients at the same hospital. Mean age 70 years, 56% male, 80% with fall as mechanism of injury.
595.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

596.title: Acute mountain sickness: Lake Louise Score
596.reference: Meier D, et al. Does this patient have acute mountain sickness? The Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review. JAMA 2017: 318: 1810-19.
596.population: Systematic review of multiple clinical prediction rules, which used a Lake Louise Score ≥ 5 as the reference standard.
596.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

597.title: Pneumonia prognosis (CRB-65)
597.reference: Ebell MH, et al. Meta-analysis of Calibration, Discrimination, and Stratum-Specific Likelihood Ratios for the CRB-65 Score. J Gen Intern Med. 2019 Jul;34(7):1304-1313
597.population: Systematic review of 8 high quality clinical prediction rule validation studies. Only studies of adults presenting to an outpatient setting were included. LR and PV are based on 4% absolute mortality risk, using data from subset of studies where patients could be treated as inpatient or outpatients.
597.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

598.title: Predicting recurrent VTE (HERDOO2 rule)
598.reference: Rodger MA, LeGal G, Anderson DR, et al. Validating the HERDOO2 rule to guide treatment duration for women with unprovoked venous thrombosis: multinational prospective cohort management study. BMJ 2017; 356: j1065
598.population: Validation study with 1214 women who received anticoagulation following unprovoked VTE for 5 to 12 months, and were followed for one year following discontinuation of anticoagulation.
598.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

599.title: Predicting major bleeding in anticoagulated patients with VTE (VTE-BLEED score)
599.reference: Klok FA, et al. External validation of the VTE bleed score for predicting major bleeding in stable anticoagulated patients with venous thromboembolism. Thromb Haemost 2017; 117; 1165-70.
599.population: Validation study using RCT comparing heparin followed by edoxaban or a LMWH. Follow-up was < 3 months for 12%, 3-12 months for 47%, and 12 months for 40%; mean age 56 years, 70% white, 21% Asian, 4% African. Study primarily focused on major bleeds after 30 days (during stable anticoagulation).
599.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

600.title: Predicting alcoholic cause of steatohepatitis (ALD/NAFLD Index or ANI)
600.reference: Dunn W, et al. Utility of a New Model to Diagnose an Alcohol Basis for Steatohepatitis. Gastroenterology. 2006 Oct; 131(4): 1057–1063.
600.population: Derived in 241 patients at Mayo Clinic, using alcohol consumption history as reference standard. Validated in 3 cohorts using previously collected data at the same institution, using some patients with cirrhosis, acute alcoholic hepatitis, confirmed NAFLD.
600.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

601.title: Predicting bacterial cause of meningitis (Meningitis Score for Emergencies or MSE)
601.reference: Mintegi S, et al. Clinical Prediction Rule for Distinguishing Bacterial From Aseptic Meningitis. Pediatrics 2020 Sep;146(3): e20201126. doi: 10.1542/peds.2020-1126.
601.population: Derived in 810 children 29 days to 14 years admitted with meningitis in 25 Spanish ED's from 2011 to 2016, validated prospectively in 190 in same setting from 2017-2018. Median age 48 months, median duration of fever 24 hours.
601.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

602.title: 0/1 hour cardiac troponin algorithm to diagnose acute MI
602.reference: McCord J, et al. The role of cardiac testing with the 0/1-hour high-sensitivity cardiac troponin algorithm evaluating for acute myocardial infarction. Am Heart J 2021 Mar; 233:68-77. doi: 10.1016/j.ahj.2020.12.015.
602.population: Prospective validation of the algorithm in patients at a single Swiss urban center. Patients were followed up at 30 and 45 days for death or acute MI. Of 45 patients with AMI, 27 were Type 1 and 18 Type 2. Of 270 in rule out zone, 1 had MACE and no deaths or AMI at 30 days (0.4%).
602.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

603.title: Predicting abuse in children based on bruising (Bruising Clinical Decision Rule or BCDR)
603.reference: Pierce MC, et al. Validation of a Clinical Decision Rule to Predict Abuse in Young Children Based on Bruising Characteristics. JAMA Netw Open 2021 Apr 1;4(4):e215832. doi: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.5832.
603.population: Prospective validation (with refinement) in 5 urban pediatric ED's in the US. Enrolled children presenting with bruising under age 4 years. Mean age 2.1 years, 60% male, 83% white. NPV 98.8%, PPV 63.9%.
603.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

604.title: Identifying patients at low risk of ACS without troponin (HEAR score)
604.reference: Moumneh T, et al. Identifying Patients with Low Risk of Acute Coronary Syndrome Without Troponin Testing: Validation of the HEAR Score. Am J Med 2021 Apr;134(4):499-506.e2. doi: 10.1016/j.amjmed.2020.09.021. Epub 2020 Oct 27.
604.population: HEAR score is a subset of HEART score minus troponin. This was a prospective validation in 22,109 adults presenting with suspected ACS to a southern California KP emergency department who had a HEART score documented. Mean age 58, 57% female, 50% white, 37% Hispanic. Patients presenting with STEMI were excluded.
604.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

605.title: Prognosis for patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (REVEAL Lite 2.0 score)
605.reference: Benza RL, et al. Development and Validation of an Abridged Version of the REVEAL 2.0 Risk Score Calculator, REVEAL Lite 2, for Use in Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension. Chest 2021 Jan; 159(1): 337–346.
605.population: This risk score was developed and internally validated in 2529 patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. Most were NYHA II or III with a mean age of 54 years and 80% were female; 50% had idiopathic disease.

606.title: Risk of cardiogenic shock with STEMI treated with PCI (ORBI risk score)
606.reference: Auffret V, et al. Predicting the development of in-hospital cardiogenic shock in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction treated by primary percutaneous coronary intervention: the ORBI risk score. Eur Heart J 2018 Jun 7;39(22):2090-2102.
606.population: The risk score was developed in a group of 6838 patients with primary PCI for STEMI in France (Observatoire Regional Breton sur l'Infarctus or ORBI) from 2006 to 2015. It was then validated in 2208 patients with acute MI in 2 cardiac ICUs in the Cote-d'Or region of France between 2002 and 2016. Mean age was 64 years in the validation cohort, 29% female, and 43% had anterior MI. Cardiogenic shock was more common in the validation group (8.3% vs 4.3%).
606.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

607.title: Risk of organ-specific recurrence after colon cancer resection
607.reference: Nagata H, et al. Development and Validation of a Prediction Model for Organ-Specific Recurrences After Curative Resection of Colon Cancer. Dis Colon Rectum 2019 Sep; 62 (9): 1043-1054. doi: 10.1097 / DCR.0000000000001430.
607.population: The risk score was developed in 973 patients treated from 1997-2009, and validated in 747 patients at the same Japanese institution from 2010 to 2015. All data were retrospectively obtained from the health record. The mean age in the validation cohort was 68 years, 58% were men, and 70% of patients underwent laparoscopic surgery.
607.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation
607.comment: In the validation cohort, 7.7% developed liver metastasis and 3.6% lung metastasis.

608.title: Delirium assessment in older hospitalized adults (4AT risk score)
608.reference: Shenkin S, et al. Delirium detection in older acute medical inpatients: a multicentre prospective comparative diagnostic test accuracy study of the 4AT and the confusion assessment method. BMC Medicine 2019 Jul 24;17(1):138.
608.population: Prospective validation of 421 adults 70 years and older hospitalized < 96 hours or in ED < 12 hours. Reference standard was based on detailed neuropsych assessment by the researchers. Mean age 81 years, 55% female, 14% with dementia diagnosis, only 7% evaluated in ED.
608.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
608.comment: Also validated in study of 419 ED patients (Age and Ageing 2018; 47: 61-68) with good discrimination and calibration.

609.title: Likelihood of true penicillin allergy (PEN-FAST score)
609.reference: Trubiano JA, Vogrin S, Chua KYL, Bourke J, Yun J, Douglas A, et al. Development and Validation of a Penicillin Allergy Clinical Decision Rule. JAMA Intern Med. 2020;180(5):745–52.
609.population: The risk score was derived from a prospective cohort of 622 allergy-tested patients in Australia, using a logistic regression model. External validation was performed in multicentre retrospective cohorts in Australia (Perth, N=334; Sydney, N= 80) and the United States of America (Nashville, TN, N=531) with 94% undergoing oral penicillin challenge and the remainder skin prick/intradermal testing alone. Calibration and discrimination were excellent.
609.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

610.title: Identifying patients at very low risk for acute MI (Mini GRACE score)
610.reference: Tscherny K, et al. Early identification of patients with chest pain at very low risk of acute myocardial infarction using clinical information and ECG only. Int J Clin Pract 2020; 74: e13526
610.population: The risk score was drawn from the GRACE score for acute MI, dropping the biomarkers and leaving only vital signs, history, and ECG. Mean age 69, 24% female, 25% prior PCI, 23% prior MI, 4% prior CABG. The study population included anyone presenting to the ED with new onset chest pain, dyspnoea, change in exercise tolerance, or any other angina equivalent. Patients already diagnosed with MI by EMS or referral hospital were excluded.
610.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

611.title: Diagnosis of cellulitis (ALT70 score)
611.reference: Raff AB, Weng QY, Cohen JM, et al. A predictive model for diagnosis of lower extremity cellulitis: A cross-sectional study.–J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017;76(4):618-625.e2. doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2016.12.044
611.population: The ALT-70 score was developed using a retrospective chart review of 259 patients of whom 70% had a final diagnosis of cellulitis. It had similar predictive value for inpatients at 24 and 48 hours after admission, based on a retrospective chart review. It has been validated prospectively, and it outperformed thermal imaging for the diagnosis of lower extremity cellulitis in the emergency department (ED).6 In that study of 67 patients, using dermatology consult as the reference standard.
611.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

612.title: Likelihood of 30-day MACE in patients with chest pain in ED (EDACS score)
612.reference: Boyle R, et al. The Diagnostic Accuracy of the Emergency Department Assessment of Chest Pain (EDACS) Score: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Ann Emerg Med 2021 Apr;77(4):433-441.
612.population: Systematic review of 8 diagnostic accuracy studies and one RCT with a total of 12,136 patients. Summary estimate of sensitivity was 96.1% and specificity was 61.1%. Identified 6370 (55%) of patients as low risk, of whom 61 (0.54%) had a major adverse cardiac event in the next 30 days.
612.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

613.title: Likelihood of stroke with chronic atrial fibrillation (modified CHADS2 score)
613.reference: Rietbrock S, et al. Chronic atrial fibrillation: Incidence, prevalence, and prediction of stroke using the Congestive heart failure, Hypertension, Age > 75, Diabetes mellitus, and prior Stroke or transient ischemic attack (CHADS2) risk stratification scheme. Am Heart J 2008 Jul;156(1):57-64. doi: 10.1016/j.ahj.2008.03.010
613.population: Case-control study evaluating both CHADS2 and this modification which identifies more age strata and drops some variables. Patients were followed a median of 2.5 years, half were women, and median age was approximately 75 years.
613.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
613.comment: A more recent validation study found that for patients with atrial fib and impaired renal function, the modified CHADS2 was the best predictor of stroke risk (Eur Heart J 2021; 42: 1476-85).

614.title: Delirium assessment in older hospitalized adults (4AT risk score)
614.reference: Shenkin S, et al. Delirium detection in older acute medical inpatients: a multicentre prospective comparative diagnostic test accuracy study of the 4AT and the confusion assessment method. BMC Medicine 2019 Jul 24;17(1):138.
614.population: Prospective validation of 421 adults 70 years and older hospitalized < 96 hours or in ED < 12 hours. Reference standard was based on detailed neuropsych assessment by the researchers. Mean age 81 years, 55% female, 14% with dementia diagnosis, only 7% evaluated in ED.
614.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
614.comment: Also validated in study of 419 ED patients (Age and Ageing 2018; 47: 61-68) with good discrimination and calibration.

615.title: Pediatric blunt abdominal injury - probability of CT finding requiring intervention
615.reference: Holmes JF, et al. Identifying Children at Very Low Risk of Clinically Important Blunt Abdominal Injuries. Ann Emerg Med 2013; 62(2): 107- 116 AND Springer E, et al. External validation of a clinical prediction rule for very low risk pediatric blunt abdominal trauma. Am J Emerg Med 2019; 37: 1643-9.
615.population: Derived using data from children with blunt torso trauma presenting within 24 hours to one of 20 emergency departments in the US PECARN network. It was then prospectively validated (Am J Emerg Med 2019; 37: 1643-8) in a population of 5743 chilren with blunt abdominal trauma, which found essentially identical results to the derivation group.
615.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

616.title: Febrile infant < 60 days at low risk for SBI (PECARN Febrile Infant Rule)
616.reference: Kuppermann N, et al. A clinical prediction rule to identify febrile infants 60 days and younger at low risk for serious bacterial infections. JAMA Pediatrics 2019; 173: 342-51.
616.population: Prospective external validation of a clinical prediction rule to identify infants < 60 days presenting to ED with fever who are at low risk of serious bacterial infection (SBI). SBI was defined as UTI, bacteremia, or bacterial meningitis.
616.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
616.comment: Performance in derivation, internal validation, and external validation groups was nearly identical. Out of over 3000 infants no cases of bacterial meningitis were missed.

617.title: Cardiogenic syncope prediction (EGSYS score)
617.reference: Del Rosso A, et al. Clinical predictors of cardiac syncope at initial evaluation in patients referred urgently to a general hospital: the EGSYS score. Heart 2008; 94(12):1620-6
617.population: Prospective external validations of a risk score for predicting cardiogenic syncope. Validation 1: 198 ED patients in Iran with syncope, mean age 59, 62% male, 58% cardiac syncope. Validation 2: 260 ED patients with unexplained syncope in Italy.
617.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

618.title: Sudden arrhythmic death risk in patients with coronary disease
618.reference: Chatterjee NA, et al. Simple electrocardiographic measures improve sudden arrhythmic death prediction in coronary disease. Eur Soc Cardiol 2020; 41: 1988-99
618.population: Derived in the PRE-DETERMINE study population of patients with coronary disease on angiography or previous MI, including some with mild to moderate heart failure. Mean age 64, 77% male, 89% white. Validated in ARTEMIS trial population of patients with angiographically confirmed coronary disease, mean age 67 years, 68% female, 100% white.
618.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

619.title: Lower respiratory tract infection prognosis in outpatient adults
619.reference: Moore M, et al. Predictors of adverse outcomes in uncomplicated lower respiratory tract infections. Ann Fam Med 2019; 17: 231-8.
619.population: Participants were primary care patients in 522 UK practices presenting with acute cough and not referred to hospital; 29% 60 and older, 61% female, 53% short of breath, 48% purulent sputum, 29% fever.
619.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

620.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus diagnostic criteria (EULAR 2019)
620.reference: Aringer M, et al. 2019 European League Against Rheumatism/American College of Rheumatology classification criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus. Arthr & Rheum 2019; 71: 1400-12.
620.population: A Delphi developed the initial set of criteria. This was then refined and simplified in a derivation cohort of 1001 subjects and validated in a second group of 1200 subjects with clinically suspected SLE.
620.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

621.title: Opioid induced respiratory depression among inpatients (PRODIGY)
621.reference: Khanna AK, et al. Prediction of opioid-induced respiratory depression on inpatient wards using continuous capnography and oximetry: an international prospective, observational trial. Anesthesia & Analgesia 2020; 131: 1012.
621.population: Adults in US, Europe, Japan and Singapore expected to receive parenteral opioid therapy on a general medical floor and able to wear continuous monitoring equipment. Mean age 60 years, about 95% were surgical patients. Respiratory depression event defined as RR <= 5 bpm, O2 sat < 85%, or end-tidal CO2 <= 15 or ≥ 60 mm Hg, all for at least 3 minutes; or apnea > 30 seconds.
621.validation: Quality score 4 (1-4): No independent validation; rule validated on same data used to develop it.

622.title: Pneumonia: need for intensive respiratory or vasopressor support (SMART-COP)
622.reference: Charles PG, SMART-COP: a tool for predicting the need for intensive respiratory or vasopressor support in community-acquired pneumonia. Clin Infect Dis 2008; 47: 375.
622.population: Developed in prospective Australian cohort of patients hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia; 24% 50 years or younger, 61% male, full range of pneumonia severity by PSI and CRB-65. Validated in 5 external databases.
622.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

623.title: Hospitalization risk in patients with diabetes mellitus
623.reference: Berg DB, et al. A biomarker-based score for risk of hospitalization for heart failure in patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care 2021; 44 https://doi.org/10.2337/dc21-1170
623.population: Developed in the SAVOR-TIMI 53 trial of patients with T2DM and coronary disease, and validated in the DECLARE-TIMI 58 population. T2DM was well controlled (A1C 7 to 8) , 10% to 13% had heart failure by history, and mean age 61-67 years by baseline troponin group. Validation cohort was followed for 4.2 years.
623.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

624.title: Mortality in acute upper and lower GI bleed (ABC score)
624.reference: Laursen SB, et al. ABC score: a new risk score that accurately predicts mortality in acute upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding: an international multicentre study. Gut 2021; 70: 707-16.
624.population: Developed in a prospective cohort of 3012 patients with acute upper GI bleed in US, UK, Denmark, and New Zealand. Validated in two populations, one with 4019 patients with upper GI bleed in Israel, Italy, and Spain and a second with 2336 UK patients with lower GI bleed. Mortality in the validation cohorts ranged from 4.1% to 9.6% for upper GI bleed and was 2.3% for lower GI bleed.
624.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

625.title: Cerebral venous thrombosis risk score
625.reference: Heldner MR, et al. Prediction of cerebral venous thrombosis with a new clinical score and d-dimer levels. Neurology 2020; 95: e898-e909.
625.population: Prospective cohort of adults with clinically suspected cerebral venous thrombosis based on isolated unexpected headache, headache with neuro deficits, headache with disturbed consciousness, headache with seizure, or papilledema. Mean age 40 years, 70% female, and 85% white.
625.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
625.comment: Not externally validated but is only risk score on this topic.

626.title: Canadian Syncope Risk Score for serious outcomes
626.reference: Thiruganasambandamoorthy V, et al. Multicenter emergency department validation of the Canadian Syncope Risk Score. JAMA Internal Med 2020; 180: 737-44.
626.population: Prospective external validation at 9 large EDs in Canada of patients 16 and older presenting within 24 hours of syncope. Those with more than 5 minutes of loss of consciousness, mental status changes, head trauma, or observed seizure were excluded. Mean age 54, 55% female, 63% arrived by ambulance.
626.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
626.comment: A separate study compared the Canadian Syncope Risk score to three other scores and concluded that it was the most accurate (Acad Emerg Med 2021; 28: 502-10

627.title: Predicting complicated staph aureus bacteremia
627.reference: Lambregts MMC, et al. Early differentiation between uncomplicated and complicated staphylococcus aureus bacteremia: potential value and limitations of a clinical risk score. Int J Clin Pract 2020; 74: e13601
627.population: Developed in a retrospective cohort of patients presenting with staph aureus bacteremia (SAB) to a hospital in the Netherlands. Validation cohort was patients with SAB at 3 other Dutch hospitals. Complicated SAB was defined as anyone with endocarditis or metastatic infection, positive cultures after 48 hours of adequate treatment, and without relapse.
627.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

628.title: Steven-Johnson Syndrome/TEN diagnosis
628.reference: Kolitz E, et al. Validation of two predictive models designed to aid clinicians in identifying Stevens Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis: a single institution retrospective review. J Am Acad Dermatol 2022 April; 960 and Weinkle A, et al. Distinguishing Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis from clinical mimickers during inpatient dermatologic consultation-A retrospective chart review. J Am Acad Dermatol 2019; 81:749.
628.population: Patients referred to clinical dermatology consulting services at 4 hospitals for suspected Stevens Johnson Syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis were used to derive the risk score. It was validated in a separate population in Texas of patients with clinically suspected SJS/TEN. Details about the demographics are not provided.
628.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
628.comment: Both derivation and validation studies relied on retrospective chart reviiew. Link is to derivation study.

629.title: Traumatic brain injury risk with scalp hematoma (Infant Scalp Score)
629.reference: Schutzman SA, et al. The Infant Scalp Score: a validated tool to stratify risk of traumatic brain injury in infants with isolated scalp hematoma. Acad Emerg Med 2021; 28(1): 92.
629.population: Developed using the PECARN pediatric brain injury registry. Participants were younger than 1 year of age presenting with scalp hematoma, Glasgow score of 14 or 15, and no other clinical findings. Patients with neurological disorders or previous neurosurgery were excluded.
629.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

630.title: Carbon monoxide poisoning neurologic prognosis
630.reference: Kim SH, et al. Derivation and validation of a score for predicting poor neurocognitive outcomes in acute carbon monoxide poisoning. JAMA Network Open 2022; 5: e2210552
630.population: Derived in a population of patients with acute CO poisoning in Wonju, Korea, and validated in patients at a different hospital in Inchon, Korea. Patients were treated with 100% oxygen and if HbCO was > 25% were given hyperbaric oxygen. Mean age 47, 63% men, and mostly due to charcoal fires.
630.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

631.title: Appendicitis: identification of low risk children (PALabS score)
631.reference: Benito J, et al. A new clinical score to identify children at low risk for appendicitis. Am J Emerg Med 2020; 38: 554-61
631.population: Developed using retrospective chart data for children age 2 to 14 years admitted for suspected appendicitis to Cruces University Hospital in Spain. Validated prospectively in the same hospital at a later period.
631.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

632.title: Severity of hyperemesis gravidarum (PUQE)
632.reference: Lacasse A, Rey E, Ferreira E, et al. Validity of a modified Pregnancy-Unique Quantification of Emesis and Nausea (PUQE) scoring index to assess severity of nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. Am J Ob Gyn 2008; January pg 71.e1.
632.population: Women ≥ 18 years attending a Montreal hospital in the first trimester for prenatal care between 2004 and 2006.
632.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

633.title: Risk of venous thrombosis with chemotherapy (Khorana score)
633.reference: Khorana A, Kuderer NM, Culakova E, et al. Development and validation of a predictive model for chemotherapy-associated thrombosis. Blood 2008; 111: 4902-7.
633.population: Developed in patients in a cancer registry (115 US sites) who were initiating a new chemotherapy regimen between 2002 andn 2005. Validated in the same population using a split sample approach. About 40% were 65 years or older and 33% were male.
633.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

634.title: Suicide risk score (Ask Suicide Questions or ASQ score)
634.reference: Brent DA, Horowitz LM, Grupp-Phelan J, et al. Prediction of Suicide Attempts and Suicide-Related Events Among Adolescents Seen in Emergency Departments. JAMA Netw Open 2023; 6(2):e2255986. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.55986
634.population: Cohort of adolescents presenting to the emergency department, oversampled for those with psychiatric symptoms in 2017 and 2018 in the US. Of 3922 with baseline data, 2740 had 3 month follow-up.
634.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
634.comment: Of the 2740 with 3 month follow-up, 5.9% had at least one suicide attempt, 6.1% had a suicide related event, and 2.5% had both.

635.title: Risk of hospital intervention for lower GI bleed (SHA2PE score)
635.reference: Cerruti T, Maillard MH, Hugli O. Acute Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding in an Emergency Department and Performance of the SHA2PE Score: A Retrospective Observational Study. J Clin Med 2021, 10, 5476. https://doi.org/10.3390/jcm10235476.
635.population: Adults visiting the emergency department in 2017 with main complaint of hematochezia in the previous 24 hours. Median age 54, 53% male, and 39% with hematechezia observed in the ED
635.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

636.title: COVID in-hospital mortality risk (4C risk score)
636.reference: Gordon AJ, Govindarajan P, Bennett CL, et al. External validation of the 4C Mortality Score for hospitalised patients with COVID-19 in the RECOVER network. BMJ Open 2022; 12:e054700. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2021-054700
636.population: Adults hospitalized for COVID-19 infection in 27 US states plus DC. Median age 64 years, median O2 sat 92%, median CRP 10.5 mg/dl.
636.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population

637.title: COVID outpatient hospitalization risk (LOCH risk score)
637.reference: Ebell MH, Kieber-Emmons A, Hamadini R. Prospective validation of a simple risk score to predict hospitalization during the Omicron phase of COVID-19. JABFM 2023; in review
637.population: Adult outpatients in the Lehigh Valley Health System diagnosed with COVID-19 and initially managed as outpatients.
637.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
637.comment: Validation was prospective although in same population as used to develop the score.

638.title: Risk of severe alcohol withdrawal syndrome (AWTT score)
638.reference: Mahabir CA, Anderson M, Cimino J, et al. Derivation and validation of a multivariable model, the alcohol withdrawal triage tool (AWTT), for predicting severe alcohol withdrawal syndrome. Drug Alcohol Depend 2020; 209: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.drugalcdep.2020.107943
638.population: Retrospective study of adults presenting with an alcohol use disorder at an academic medical center between 2015 and 2018. Mean age 43 years, 72% white, and 70% male. Derivation and validation both used patients with complete data only.
638.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

639.title: Pancreatic cancer prognosis
639.reference: Hank T, Hinz U, Reiner T, et al. A Pretreatment Prognostic Score to Stratify Survival in Pancreatic Cancer. Ann Surg 2022; 276(6: e914.
639.population: Patients undergoing initial surgical exploration for potentially resectable pancreatic cancer in Heidelberg, Germany were included in the derivation group. Patients who had previous neoadjuvant chemotherapy or missing CRP levels preoperatively were excluded as well. Patients were recruited between 2006 and 2014. Of those undergoing surgery, 882 of 1197 had resection with curative intent and 315 exploration only. Median age 67 years, 56% male, and 68% in head of pancreas. The validation group was a similar cohort in Verona, Italy who had surgery between 2013 and 2016, with the exception that 23% were treated with neo-adjuvant chemo prior to surgery.
639.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
639.comment: Prevalence refers to 80% mortality at 41 months in the derivation cohort.

640.title: Likelihood of abnormality on CXR with non-traumatic chest pain
640.reference: Newsom C, Jeanmonod R, Woolley W, et al. Prospective Validation and Refinement of a Decision Rule to Obtain Chest X-ray in Patients With Nontraumatic Chest Pain in the Emergency Department. Acad Emerg Med 2018; 25: 650-6.
640.population: Adults presenting to one of 3 US emergency departments with a chief complaint of non-traumatic chest pain in 2013 to 2015. Median age was 52, 54% female.
640.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
640.comment: Overall 13.4% had a finding on CXR, but only 70 (6.4%) had a clinically relevant finding.

641.title: Safe discharge with lower GI bleed (Oakland Score)
641.reference: Oakland K, Jairath V, Uberoi R, et al. Derivation and validation of a novel risk score for safe discharge after acute gastrointestinal bleeding: a modeling study. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2017; 2: 635-43.
641.population: Derived in a population of 2528 adults at 143 UK hospitals who were admitted with lower GI bleeding, with a mean age of 68 years. Validated in 2 separate hospitals not part of the original audit population.
641.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
641.comment: Prevalence is percentage safely discharged. Safe discharge was defined as patients with none of the following after admission: rebleeding defined as need for transfusion or 20% or more decrease in HCT after 24 hours stablity; need for transfusion; intervention needed to control bleeding; in-hospital death; or readmission within 28 days for GI bleeding.

642.title: Prognosis in stable I non-small cell lung cancer (VALCAN-M score)
642.reference: Heiden BT, Eaton DB, Brandt WS, et al. Development and validation of the VA lung cancer mortality (VALCAN-M) score for 90 day mortality following surgical treatment of clinical stage I lung cancer. Ann Surg 2023; 278: e634
642.population: Developed (n=6825) and validated (n=2924) using a split sample approach in US veterans with clinical stage I NSCLC who underwent surgical treatment between 2006 and 2016.
642.validation: Quality score 2 (1-4): Split-sample with prospective validation

643.title: Risk of pulmonary complications following surgery (ARISCAT score)
643.reference: Mazo V, Sabate S, Canet J, et al. Prospective external validation of a predictive score for post-operative pulmonary complications. Anesthesiology 2014; 121: 219-31
643.population: Patients for external validation came from 63 centers reporting patients who underwent surgery including general, neuraxial or plexus block anesthesia. Mean age 59 years, 51% male, ASA 3 or 4 in 27%.
643.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
643.comment: Pulmonary complications included respiratory failure, suspected pulmonary infection, pleural effusion, atelectasis, pneumothorax, bronchospasm or aspiration pneumonia.

644.title: Risk of acute kidney injury after non-cardiac surgery
644.reference: Wilson TA, de Koning L, Quinn RR, et al. Derivation and external validation of a risk index for predicting acute kidney injury requiring kidney replacement therapy after noncardiac surgery. JAMA Network Open 2021; 4(8): e2121901
644.population: Derivation cohort came from the Alberta Kidney Disease Network, linked to ICD codes and procedure codes. They included all patients 18 to 95 years who had AAA repair or surgery for colorectal, liver or pancreatic disease as well as those who underwent other abdominal retroperitoneal, thoracic, vascular or MSK surgery from 2004 to 2013. The validation used an administrative database in Ontario.
644.validation: Quality score 1 (1-4): Test set from a distinct population
